Praying with Saint Charbel: intentions and prayers

Asking for Saint Charbel’s intercession means asking him to pray to God with us. Bring a personal intention or simply give thanks. The prayers below are original devotional texts written for this site, not official liturgical texts.

In this guide

  1. How to begin
  2. A prayer for today
  3. For someone who is ill
  4. For family and peace
  5. A prayer of thanks
  6. After prayer

How to begin

Find a quiet place and make the Sign of the Cross. Name your intention silently or in a low voice; you do not need to publish it or enter it into a form. Read a prayer slowly, then leave a little space for silence.

A prayer for today

Lord Jesus, I place this day in your hands. Through Saint Charbel’s intercession, teach me to listen, serve humbly, and return to you when my attention wanders. Help me recognize the good I can do today and give me strength to begin. Amen.

For someone who is ill

God of mercy, I entrust to you the person who is suffering and everyone caring for them. Give them comfort, hope, and strength. Guide their caregivers and help us remain present with love and respect. Saint Charbel, pray with us for them and their family. Amen.

For family and peace

Lord, accompany our families in their joys and difficulties. Teach us to speak honestly, listen patiently, and take steps toward reconciliation. Support those separated from loved ones. Let our homes become places of mercy and mutual care. Amen.

A prayer of thanks

Thank you, Lord, for the people who support me and the small signs of hope in my day. Teach me to receive your gifts humbly and share them generously. Through Saint Charbel’s intercession, keep my heart attentive to others. Amen.

After prayer

You may finish with the Our Father and a practical act of kindness. Prayer does not impose an outcome on God. Supporting someone who is ill also means respecting their care and choices. For a longer rhythm of prayer, explore the nine-day reflection guide.
